crash_hull.source: Points that hit the ground first (le frame): wing tips (60 in span, slight dihedral), spinner tip (firewall 6.94 in ahead of LE plus engine and spinner), tail end and stabilizer tips (52 in overall length), fin top, belly under the CG (fuselage bottom 0.053 m below the thrust line, from the model team's fuselage stations). Read from the Jensen plan and the visual model. Since E1 the wheels are landing_gear contacts, not hull points: a wheel on the ground is a landing, a leg pushed past its travel is a crash

landing_gear.description: E1: the wheels as spring-damper contacts with the flat ground (physics/ground_contact.gd): F_up = max(0, k·compression + c·rate) at each wheel bottom. Stiffness from the ROADMAP E1 rule ω·dt < 0.1 (ω = sqrt(Σk/m) at the 240 Hz tick), checked by the loader; the CG must lie inside the wheel footprint. E2: tyre forces in the ground plane along each wheel's heading: rolling resistance C_rr·N and a slip-angle side force saturating at μ·N (friction circle); the nose wheel steers with the rudder servo. Coefficients are for a tyre on dry pavement; per-surface factors (grass) come with the field surfaces (E3). Brakes: none.

position.source: Wheel bottoms. x from the D9d hull: mains 0.094 m aft of the plan CG, nose 0.257 m ahead (tricycle: the CG sits 27 % of the wheelbase from the mains, so the airplane stands on its nose wheel). Track 0.36 m and heights from the model team's ugly_stik_geometry.gd equipment table (axle 0.22 m below the thrust line, wheel radius 0.0381 m). NOTE for the model team: that table places the main axle at x_aft 0.10 m, AHEAD of the CG (0.1209 m); built so, the airplane would sit on its tail. Physics keeps the hull's 0.215 m until the plan is re-read

stiffness.source: ROADMAP E1 rule: ω·dt < 0.1 at 240 Hz → Σk < 1662 N/m for 2.885 kg. Mains 560 N/m, nose 440 N/m: Σ 1560 N/m, ω 23.3 rad/s (3.7 Hz), static sag 18 mm, like a wire leg plus a foam tyre; the split (nose 27 % of the weight, mains 73 %) makes the airplane sit level (test_ground_contact: rests within 1°). Not measured; a stiffer measured gear needs a finer tick or substeps

damping.source: damping ratio ζ ≈ 0.4 of the contact's share m/3: c = 2ζ·sqrt(k·m/3). A bent wire leg and a tyre damp little; structural guess, not measured

max_compression.source: leg splay before the wire bends permanently or the belly (0.053 m below the thrust line; wheels 0.258 m) hits: a level touchdown at 2 m/s sink compresses ≈ 0.10 m, at 3 m/s ≈ 0.15 m (½mv² = ½Σkδ² plus the 18 mm static sag), so 2 m/s lands and 3 m/s breaks the gear. Guess from RC practice

max_steering.source: Nose wheel steering at full rudder, linked to the rudder servo. RC tricycle setups use about 15-25° (less throw than the rudder's, to avoid swerving at speed); 20° gives a kinematic turn radius of wheelbase/tan 20° = 0.351/0.364 = 0.96 m at walking speed. Guess, not measured; JSBSim's full-size C172 uses 10°

rolling_resistance.source: Rolling resistance coefficient on dry pavement. Borrowed base 0.022 (JSBSim c172x rolling_friction, a full-size tyre on concrete), doubled for a 76 mm RC wheel (resistance grows as the wheel shrinks: deformation and bumps are larger relative to the radius). Guess; a coast-down on the owner's field would measure it (E2 report)

side_friction.source: Peak tyre friction coefficient μ on dry pavement: JSBSim c172x static_friction 0.8 (github.com/JSBSim-Team/jsbsim, aircraft/c172x/c172x.xml). One value for side force and friction circle (JSBSim's 0.5 dynamic friction for a skid is not modelled). Grass is lower (E3, field surfaces)

peak_slip_angle.source: Slip angle where the side force reaches μ·N in our linear-then-saturated law. Matches the initial slope of JSBSim's default Pacejka side-force curve (FGLGear: stiffness 0.06/deg, shape 2.8, curvature 1.03; slope at zero μ·2.8·0.06 per degree, so μ is reached linearly at 1/0.168 = 5.95°). A small RC wheel's real curve is unmeasured. Also sets the low-speed damping the loader checks: μ·g·dt/(tan 6°·1 m/s) = 0.31 at 240 Hz

breakaway_factor.source: E3b1: static ÷ rolling resistance of a wheel at rest (bearing and axle friction, tyre flat spot, the small mound in front of a wheel parked on grass). The ground knowledge base (docs/research/roadmap-investigations/04, §3) brackets it at 1.0-1.5 without a measurement; 1.25 is the middle. On the mown runway the hold is 1.25 × 2.8 N = 3.5 N against 2.6 N of idle thrust; on dry pavement 1.4 N, so the Stik rolls at idle there. A luggage-scale pull on the owner's field (breakaway force, then the steady rolling force) would measure it

mass_range.source: Stick-family .60 manuals: Ultra Stick .60 6-7 lb, Big Stik .60 6.5 lb (RESEARCH.md), widened

inertia_reference.source: UltraStick25e Jxx Jyy Jzz (1.959 kg, 1.27 m span); compared after scaling by m·b²

aileron.source: Not on the Jensen plan or in its notes; typical low-rate sport throw used since Stage 1 (formerly app/spec.gd CONTROLS). Open research track: control throws (ROADMAP)

elevator.source: Not on the Jensen plan or in its notes; typical low-rate sport throw used since Stage 1 (formerly app/spec.gd CONTROLS). Open research track: control throws (ROADMAP)

rudder.source: Not on the Jensen plan or in its notes; typical low-rate sport throw used since Stage 1 (formerly app/spec.gd CONTROLS). Open research track: control throws (ROADMAP)

servo_full_throw_time.source: Time for a surface to go from neutral to full throw: a standard analog servo at 0.19 s/60 deg (Hitec HS-311 / Futaba S3003 class at 6 V) times about 45 deg of servo-arm travel for full surface throw (typical linkage). Same for every surface

aero.source: OpenFlightSim UltraStick25e AeroOpenFlight.xml @ b020511 (sha256 43ff5c1e…); nondimensional, applied to the Ugly Stik as a geometrically similar Stik; Cmq, CLq and Cnr derived from the Stik itself (D11g)

CL_max.source: Whole-airplane maximum lift: mid value of the CLmax 1.0-1.2 assumed in the ROADMAP predicted-handling table (semi-symmetric Jensen section, Re about 3e5); gives a 1-g stall near 9.0 m/s

CL_min.source: Negative stall of a semi-symmetric section is weaker than the positive one; assumed about 0.7 x CL_max

stall_blend_width.source: Width of the smooth transition from attached flow to flat-plate flow (PicaSim uses a cosine ramp of about 10 deg, YASim a stall-width parameter); the start is solved so the lift peak equals CL_max

CD90.source: Flat-plate drag of the finite wing at 90 deg: Viterna CDmax = 1.11 + 0.018 AR with AR = b^2/S = 5.0 (NASA CR-1983, RESEARCH.md plan review #3)

sideslip_blend.source: Sideslip range where the linear beta terms (CYb, Clb, Cnb) give way to their sin(beta) form, finite and restoring up to knife edge

conventions.rates: p_hat = p·b/(2V), q_hat = q·c/(2V), r_hat = r·b/(2V)
conventions.elevator: per radian, positive = trailing edge DOWN (dCm/dElev < 0)
conventions.aileron: per radian per surface, positive = trailing edge DOWN; right and left listed separately
conventions.rudder: per radian, positive = trailing edge LEFT (dCn/dRud < 0)
conventions.axes: lift, drag, side force in wind axes; roll, pitch, yaw moments in body axes about the aero reference point

CLq.source: research/aero/d11g/derive_rate_derivatives.gd (D11g): the Stik's verified local model at the 15 m/s level trim, about the CG, downwash settled; closed form 2*a_f*(S_t/S)*(l_t/c) = 3.13; the borrowed UltraStick 25e value was 6.1639

CYdr.source: docs/research/flight-repair-implementation.md: provisional surface model; estimated, not measured flight data; CYdr=a_v*S_v/S*tau; Cndr=-CYdr*l/b; Cldr=CYdr*(z_v-z_ARP)/b; Cnb=a_v*S_v/S*l/b

Cldr.source: docs/research/flight-repair-implementation.md: provisional surface model; estimated, not measured flight data; CYdr=a_v*S_v/S*tau; Cndr=-CYdr*l/b; Cldr=CYdr*(z_v-z_ARP)/b; Cnb=a_v*S_v/S*l/b

Cmq.source: research/aero/d11g/derive_rate_derivatives.gd (D11g): the Stik's verified local model at the 15 m/s level trim, about the CG, downwash settled; the downwash lag adds Cmadot -3.59 as a state (E0a2b), so Cmq+Cmadot = -11.07; closed-form tail -7.40; the borrowed UltraStick 25e value -13.5664 lumped both

Cnb.source: docs/research/flight-repair-implementation.md: provisional surface model; estimated, not measured flight data; CYdr=a_v*S_v/S*tau; Cndr=-CYdr*l/b; Cldr=CYdr*(z_v-z_ARP)/b; Cnb=a_v*S_v/S*l/b

Cnr.source: research/aero/d11g/derive_rate_derivatives.gd (D11g): the Stik's verified local model at the 15 m/s level trim, about the CG, downwash settled; fin -2*(l_v/b)*Cnb_fin plus wing profile -CD0/3 = -0.1324 (D11f); the borrowed UltraStick 25e value -0.1833 contradicts the fin-derived Cnb

downwash_gradient.source: E0a2: dε/dα at the horizontal tail point from a flat-wing vortex lattice of the AR 5 rectangular wing (docs/research/roadmap-investigations/02-aerodynamics-rc-scale.md T2: VLM 0.457; elliptic estimate 2·CLα/(πA) = 0.50). With it the tail's free slope is lift_slope/(1 − dε/dα) = 3.22/rad, which a Helmbold tail of AR 3.27 with η 0.9 also gives (3.17); downwash follows the wing's lift, pitch rate and elevator do not. Not measured

propulsion.description: D5 thrust v0: engine rpm follows throttle with a first-order lag; thrust and torque from propeller coefficients at the current advance ratio. In-flight prop unloading (rpm rising with airspeed) waits for the shaft model (G2).

max_rpm_static.source: power balance: engine power assumed linear in rpm below the peak (estimated) = static prop power Cp·ρ·n³·D⁵ with Cp 0.0471 → n = sqrt(P_peak/n_peak / (Cp·ρ·D⁵))

lag_time_constant.source: first-order throttle response of a glow engine; replace with a throttle-step measurement

propeller.name: APC 12x6 Sport (LP12060)
propeller.rotation: clockwise seen from behind (standard tractor): the reaction torque rolls the airplane left

ct_table.source: UIUC propeller database vol. 1, measured APC Sport 11x6: apcsp_11x6_static_rd0488.txt (sha256 911866f1…) and apcsp_11x6_rd0495_6000.txt (sha256 987b1268…); applied to the 12x6 Sport by T = Ct·ρ·n²·D⁴ (APC's own 12x6 file is not reachable here); J = 0 row from the static run at 5,954 rpm, linear between J = 0 and 0.373 (no measurements there)

cp_table.source: UIUC propeller database vol. 1, measured APC Sport 11x6: apcsp_11x6_static_rd0488.txt (sha256 911866f1…) and apcsp_11x6_rd0495_6000.txt (sha256 987b1268…); applied to the 12x6 Sport by T = Ct·ρ·n²·D⁴ (APC's own 12x6 file is not reachable here)

rotating_inertia.source: Propeller + spinner + crankshaft about the shaft, for gyroscopic precession: APC Sport 12x6 about 37 g as a rod (m L^2 / 12 = 2.9e-4) plus spinner, nut and crankshaft (about 0.6e-4). Turns clockwise seen from behind (+x)

thrust_line_offset.source: thrust line through the CG height (plan: thrust line close to the fuselage centre); [x_aft, y_right, z_up] from the CG
